Prevention: As seeds can travel on animals and machinery, do not allow animals into an affected area, limit machinery use in the area and keep machinery clean to prevent spread.
Do not allow livestock to graze in infested pasture – seeds can pass through digestive tract unharmed
Clean shoes, clothing and hair after being in a potentially infested area.
The bristly one-seeded pod segments are sticky
Ensure uncontaminated water is used when flooding rice paddys as pod segments float and can be transported by water
Monitoring: Regularly check sites such as machinery tracks, grazing places, previously flooded areas fallen dry for seeds and any seedling establishment
Check for any seed germination at the start and end of the wet season
Spreading, multi-stemmed, thorny shrub usually up to 2 m tall.
The inflorescences, containing up to 100 flowers, flowers are pale pink and arranged in fluffy, globular clusters (10-20 mm across)
The fruit is an elongated and flattened pod covered in bristly hairs and up to 15 cm long and clustered at the stem tips
The plant is evergreen and bears bipinnate (twice-compound), sensitive leaves, up to 18 cm in length.
When touched they fold together and also during the night
Recurved spines (to 7 mm long) are located on the undersides of the petioles, petioules and stems
Direct Control: Direct Control
Uproot plants by hand-pulling or using machinery, and destroy roots
Collect seeds and burn before weeding
Cut plants off at 10 cm below ground level to kill the weed.
Use long handled cutters, axe or machete:
Blade ploughing is effective since it cuts below ground level.
Slashing and chaining alone is not (requires herbicide application afterwards)
Burning is not recommended – does not prevent resprouting and kills only surface seeds.
It may stimulate germination.
Also reduces the numbers of the stem-mining moth
Carmenta mimosa .
Check which biocontrols are available in your country.
Examples of biological controls include:
Beetle species such as
Acanthoscelides puniceus or
A. quadridentatus
The green twig-mining moth
Neurostrota gunniella attacks mature plants and seedlings greater than 15 cm (should not be used in
Thailand or
Vietnam).
You can use this after weed removal to reduce herbicide use
Fragment infestations to increase numbers of control agents such as
N. gunniella since it increases weed stand edges
